claims.text: The material family of interest is multiphase, BCC-based refractory high-entropy alloys, and the primary mechanical property is ductility measured by elongation or strain to failure.
BCC-matrix RHEAs containing ordered B2 precipitates will undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
The initial microstructure consists of a disordered BCC matrix with incipient or weakly ordered B2 precipitates.
Initial ductility arises primarily from deformation and strain hardening of the disordered BCC matrix.
Aging at approximately 700–900 °C induces phase separation, B2 or L21 chemical ordering, loss of coherency, and eventual formation of a reticulated secondary-phase network.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer, reduce stress concentration, and suppress interfacial cracking.
Increasing chemical order and losing interface coherency increase strength while reducing ductility through restricted dislocation motion and interfacial decohesion.
A continuous reticulated Laves-phase structure can impede crack extension.
The reticulated Laves phase in HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 is associated with ductile dimples in the Laves phase and quasi-cleavage in BCC grains.
At long aging times, formation of a reticulated brittle-phase network restores ductility after an intermediate brittle state.
Elongation will first decrease as ordering and incoherency develop and then increase when the secondary phase becomes reticulated.
Whether the proposed transition occurs depends on the volume fraction and connectivity of the secondary phase.
A Laves phase can form a crack-impeding reticulated network at a volume fraction of about 3.8% in HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5.
Heusler phases are capable of forming the reticulated network required for the proposed ductility recovery.
The BCC matrix must retain sufficient intrinsic ductility for both the initial and final ductile states.
A Pugh ratio K/G greater than 1.75 is an indicator of intrinsic ductility in a BCC RHEA.
Prior evidence needed to support the hypothesis includes direct measurements of chemical order, interface coherency, secondary-phase connectivity, and their evolution with aging time.
The proposed test uses an unaged condition and specimens aged at 800 °C for 10–500 hours, followed by microscopy, diffraction, and room-temperature tensile testing.
A monotonic ductility curve across all aging times would falsify the proposed ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
A significant ductility increase while the secondary phase remains isolated or granular would falsify the proposed reticulated-network mechanism.

contradictions.description: The target is initially defined around ordered B2 precipitates, but the proposed recovery boundary and exemplar rely on Laves or Heusler phases. These are distinct phase types, and no B2-to-Laves/Heusler transformation or coexistence pathway is specified.

An ordered, incoherent precipitate network is described as causing stress concentration and interfacial cracking, while a later continuous reticulated brittle-phase network is described as impeding cracks. The hypothesis does not clearly define the topological or interfacial distinction that reverses the effect of network formation.
